I reviewed the documentation for `report-builder` v2.1.0. That means `README.md`, which I checked against `package.json` and `src/main.js`. The `.claude/skills/` folder holds agent tooling, not project docs, so I left it out.

**Audience:** I assumed the readers are developers who want to run the report builder on their own machine. The README only has *Requirements* and *Build* sections, and `package.json` only defines run and test scripts.

The README is very short, and two of its few claims don't match the code.

## Classification

| Page | Intended form | Actual form | User need it should serve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `README.md` | Landing page plus quick-start how-to | A one-line summary and one run instruction; no setup or usage | "What is this, and how do I get a report out of it?" |

## Findings

| Severity | Location | Evidence | Suggested fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocker | `README.md:11`, `package.json:7-10` | The README says to run `npm run build`, but `package.json` has no `build` script. It only has `start` and `test`. A reader following the README will hit npm's "Missing script" error on the first step. | Remove `npm run build`, because `start` runs `src/main.js` directly. Or add the `build` script if one is meant to exist. |
| blocker | `README.md:7`, `package.json:5` | The README says "Node.js 18 or later", but `engines.node` is `>=22`. Users on Node 18–21 will meet the requirement as written and still be unsupported. | Change the README to "Node.js 22 or later". `engines` should be the single source for this, and the README should match it. |
| major | `README.md:3`, `src/main.js:1` | The README says the tool "builds weekly usage reports from the events table". The code only does `console.log('report')`. It reads no table, has no database connection, and has no weekly logic. The README also doesn't say which events table, how to connect to it, or what a report looks like and where it goes. | Describe what the tool actually does today. If the events table is coming later, document the data source, connection settings, and output once the code exists. Until then, don't claim it. |
| major | `README.md` (whole page) | There is no usage section at all: no settings, environment variables, arguments, or example output. Readers can't tell whether a run worked. | Add a "Run a report" how-to with numbered steps, a fenced command, and sample output. |
| minor | `README.md:9-11` | The heading "Build" covers both building and running. The steps are in a sentence, not a numbered list, and the commands aren't in a fenced `bash` block, so they're harder to copy. | Rename the heading to "Build and run" or "Run the report builder". Use numbered steps with a fenced `bash` block. |
| minor | `README.md`, `package.json:9` | The `npm test` script isn't documented. There are also no test files, so `node --test` finds nothing to run. | Add a "Run the tests" section once tests exist. |
| minor | `README.md:3` | "events table" is jargon the page never defines. "weekly usage" doesn't say whose usage or which week. | Define the data source in plain words at first use. |
| minor | `README.md` | There's no owner, maintainer or support contact, no CODEOWNERS file, no changelog for v2.1.0, and no licence. This isn't a git repository, so I can't suggest an owner from history. | Add a maintainer or support section, and a changelog if v2.x releases go to users. |

## Strengths

- There is a single `H1`, headings don't skip levels, and they're in sentence case.
- The first sentence says what the tool does, so the page passes the three-second test, even though the claim itself is wrong.
- Prerequisites come before the steps that need them.
- There are no bare-URL or "click here" links, and no images, tables or secrets.

## Suggested diffs

```diff
 ## Requirements

-- Node.js 18 or later
+- Node.js 22 or later

-## Build
+## Run the report builder

-Run `npm run build`, then `npm start`.
+```bash
+npm start
+```
```

The line on `README.md:3` needs to be decided against what the tool is meant to do, so I haven't proposed wording for it.

## Unevaluated

- **Commands:** I didn't run `npm run build`, `npm start` or `npm test`, because this session doesn't allow running commands. The two blockers come from reading the files, not from running them.
- **Linters:** The repo has no linter config (no markdownlint, Vale or link-checker setup), and I couldn't run any tools anyway.
- **Links:** The README has no links, internal or external, so there was nothing to check.
- **Freshness:** There's no git history, so I couldn't check when the README was last updated.
- **Report check:** I didn't save this report or run `scripts/check-review-report.mjs` on it, because this session doesn't allow writing files or running scripts.
